adventure.definition: An exciting or unusual experience, often involving travel or risk.
adventure.example: The camping trip became an unforgettable adventure.

alphabet.definition: The set of letters used for writing a language, arranged in a fixed order.
alphabet.example: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.

ancient.definition: Very old; belonging to a time long ago.
ancient.example: We studied an ancient civilization in class.

audience.definition: The group of people watching or listening to a performance or event.
audience.example: The audience applauded at the end of the play.

breathe.definition: To take air into the lungs and let it out again.
breathe.example: Breathe slowly before you begin your speech.

ceiling.definition: The inside surface at the top of a room.
ceiling.example: A fan was attached to the ceiling.

certainly.example: I will certainly help you with the project.

chocolate.definition: A sweet food made from cocoa, often eaten as candy or used in desserts.
chocolate.example: She shared a piece of chocolate with her friend.

classroom.definition: A room where students are taught.
classroom.example: The students decorated their classroom for the event.

comfortable.definition: Feeling relaxed and physically at ease.
comfortable.example: These shoes are comfortable enough for a long walk.

creature.definition: A living being, especially an animal.
creature.example: A tiny sea creature moved across the rock.

curious.definition: Wanting to know or learn something.
curious.example: The curious child asked many questions.

daughter.example: Their daughter is learning to play the piano.

daylight.definition: Natural light from the sun during the day.
daylight.example: We reached the campsite before daylight disappeared.

different.definition: Not the same as another person or thing.
different.example: The two pictures look similar but are slightly different.

disappear.definition: To stop being visible or to go away.
disappear.example: The rainbow began to disappear behind the clouds.

discover.definition: To find or learn something for the first time.
discover.example: Scientists continue to discover new species.

eighth.definition: In position number eight in a series.

enormous.example: An enormous tree stood in the center of the park.

environment.definition: The natural world and the conditions in which people, animals, and plants live.
environment.example: We should protect the environment by reducing waste.

foreign.definition: From or connected with another country.

furniture.definition: Large movable objects such as tables, chairs, and beds used in a room.
furniture.example: The new apartment has very little furniture.

government.definition: The group of people and system that officially control a country or region.
government.example: The government announced a new public program.

height.definition: The measurement of how tall a person or thing is.
height.example: We measured the height of the plant each week.

invitation.definition: A spoken or written request asking someone to attend an event.
invitation.example: I received an invitation to her birthday party.

knowledge.definition: Information and understanding gained through learning or experience.
knowledge.example: Reading can increase your knowledge of the world.

laughter.definition: The sound or act of laughing.

magazine.definition: A publication with articles and pictures that is issued regularly.
magazine.example: She read a science magazine on the bus.

national.definition: Related to an entire country or nation.
national.example: The national team played an important match.

newspaper.definition: A printed or digital publication that reports news and information.
newspaper.example: My grandfather reads the newspaper every morning.

orchestra.definition: A large group of musicians who play different instruments together.
orchestra.example: The orchestra performed a famous piece of music.

schedule.definition: A plan that shows the times when activities or events will happen.
schedule.example: Check the schedule to see when the next class begins.

science.definition: The study of the natural world through observation and experiments.
science.example: We did an experiment in science class.

scissors.definition: A tool with two blades used for cutting.
scissors.example: Use the scissors carefully when cutting the paper.

separate.definition: To divide or keep things apart, or existing apart from something else.
separate.example: Please separate the paper from the plastic.

september.definition: The ninth month of the year.
september.example: The new school term begins in September.

straight.definition: Without a curve or bend; in a direct line.
straight.example: Draw a straight line across the page.

strawberry.definition: A small red fruit with tiny seeds on its surface.
strawberry.example: She added a strawberry to the fruit salad.

through.definition: From one side or end of something to the other.

toothbrush.definition: A small brush used for cleaning the teeth.
toothbrush.example: Remember to replace your toothbrush regularly.

tradition.definition: A custom or belief that is passed from one generation to another.
tradition.example: Making this special meal is a family tradition.

vegetable.definition: A plant or part of a plant that is eaten as food.

volleyball.definition: A team sport in which players hit a ball over a high net.

waterfall.definition: A place where water flows over the edge of a steep drop.
waterfall.example: The trail ended near a beautiful waterfall.

whole.example: She read the whole book in one weekend.
